exposure: extremes of birth weights (<2500 g, >4000 g)
cohort: Women aged 13-19 years at time of delivery who gave birth at a tertiary university hospital between July 2011 and July 2016
finding: Among adolescent patients, younger age, higher body mass index at delivery, and extremes of neonatal birth weight (both low and high) were associated with increased risk of primary nonelective cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Neonates with extreme birth weights (<2500 g, >4000 g) were more likely to be delivered via cesarean section.
